basic_info.title: GradNorm: Gradient Normalization for Adaptive Loss Balancing in Deep Multitask Networks
basic_info.affiliation: Magic Leap, Inc. (not fully confirmed from abstract page)

method.notes: Automatically re-weights per-task loss coefficients during training by equalizing the MAGNITUDE of each task's gradient at the shared representation layer, controlled by a single hyperparameter alpha (rather than requiring exhaustive manual grid search over static loss weights, which scales exponentially with task count). Directly applicable as a candidate fix for Stage-2's MDN-GPS-vs-RoadScorer competition: rather than fixed weights (lambda_mdn=1.0, lambda_road implicit at 1.0, lambda_prior_road=0.5, lambda_zonly_road=0.2), GradNorm-style dynamic re-weighting would automatically detect and counteract the GPS head's gradient dominance over the RoadScorer head as training proceeds -- directly targeting the newly observed hit@1-degrades-while-cl_gps-improves pattern.

gap_analysis.whats_missing: Not a map-matching or pillar-novelty paper -- included as a candidate Stage-2 loss-balancing mechanism.
gap_analysis.novelty_reasoning: Relevant only as a concrete, off-the-shelf mechanism to counteract gradient-magnitude imbalance between Stage-2's MDN GPS head and RoadScorer head, an alternative/complement to manually re-tuning lambda_prior_road or lambda_zonly_road by hand.

relevance.bmw_relevance: Not directly BMW-relevant; flagged as a candidate mechanism if manual loss-weight tuning (the current approach for lambda_prior_road, lambda_zonly_road, road_keep_prob) proves too brittle across further Stage-2 experiments.

uncertain: Whether GradNorm's gradient-magnitude-equalization is compatible with Stage-2's KL-based ELBO training (which already has its own free-bits/balancing mechanism) without interaction effects was not analyzed -- would need careful combination, not a drop-in replacement for the existing KL balance.
